title: Context management: token counting and compaction triggers
goal: Track how much of the model context window each agent has used and trigger compaction at sensible thresholds, surfacing 'compacting' and 'context-full' to the UI.
scope_in: `ContextTracker` per agent updated from SDK usage data (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, cache fields) after each message and from an estimator for the pending prompt (`ceil(chars / 3.5)`, replaced by real counts when available).
Model window table in config `context.windows` (default 200 000 tokens for unknown models) so new models need only config changes.
Thresholds (config, defaults): warn at 75%, auto-compact when idle at >= 85%, `context-full` at >= 97%. Hysteresis: each fires once until usage drops 10 points below it.

`compact(agentId)` asks the runner to run the SDK compaction (the `/compact` command) between turns only, never mid-tool-call; emits `agent:compaction {phase:'start'|'end', before, after}` and a `message.system` text payload (level `info`) for the transcript.
`UsageAccumulator` producing per-agent deltas `{ tokens_in, tokens_out }` consumed by the usage-events client (separate lane) with monotonic totals and no double counting after resume.
Emits `agent:context {agent_id, used, window, pct}` at most once per second per agent.
scope_out: Sending usage events to the API: billing/usage client lane.
Choosing what to drop from context (the SDK does the summarisation).
Rendering the context meter: TUI lanes.
Mapping to wire states: lane C014 turns `compaction` signals into `compacting`.
build_against: FakeSdkAdapter (lane C013) emits scripted usage numbers; fake clock; no network. Usage event shape checked against the generated `POST /v1/usage/events` request type (types `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`).
interfaces: `createContextTracker(deps: { bus: AgentBus; clock: Clock; config: ContextConfig; compact: (id: AgentId) => Promise<void> }): ContextTracker`

`interface ContextTracker { onUsage(id: AgentId, u: { model: string; input_tokens: number; output_tokens: number; cache_read_tokens?: number }): void; onPrompt(id: AgentId, chars: number): void; setIdle(id: AgentId, idle: boolean): void; snapshot(id: AgentId): { used: number; window: number; pct: number }; usageDelta(id: AgentId): { tokens_in: number; tokens_out: number } }`
acceptance: With window 200 000: usage 150 000 emits one warn (75%), 170 000 while idle triggers exactly one `compact` call, and a second update at 171 000 does not trigger again until usage drops below 150 000.
`context-full` signal fires once at 194 000 (97%) and clears after compaction reduces usage below 174 000.
Compaction is never invoked while `setIdle(id,false)` (tool running); a deferred trigger fires within one tick after `setIdle(id,true)`.
`estimateTokens(3500)` returns 1000; for any chars in [0, 10^7] the result is monotone non-decreasing (property test).
`usageDelta` totals equal the sum of reported usage across 1,000 randomly ordered updates including a resume replay of already-counted messages (message ids de-duplicate).
`agent:context` events are rate-limited to <= 1/s/agent even when 100 updates arrive in 1 s (fake clock).
Unknown model name uses the default window and logs once at debug.
guardrails: MUST NOT trigger compaction during a tool call or while an approval is pending.
MUST NOT send prompt or message text anywhere; the tracker sees only counts and model names (model names are secret on the wire and never logged).
Usage counts MUST be monotonic and de-duplicated by message id; MUST NOT report negative deltas.
All timers/intervals MUST use the injected clock and be cleared on agent exit.
failure_modes: SDK gives no usage data -> fall back to estimates, flag `estimated:true` in snapshots and skip auto-compaction (warn only).
Compaction fails -> emit `message.system` level `warn`, back off 60 s, retry at most 3 times.
Window config invalid (<= 0) -> default 200 000 with a warning.
notes: Thresholds and the 3.5 chars/token heuristic are product choices. `context-full` is a client-local UI state in CT-STATE-MAP (limits category).
